newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Egana says no plans to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: Egana says no plans to buy back shares.

text.p: Egana International (Holdings) Ltd has no immediate plans to buy back shares in the market despite recent falls in its share price, company executives said on Friday.
"We are not aware of any reason behind the recent price fluctuation and we do not have any plans to repurchase our shares in the market," executive director Peter Lee told reporters on Friday.
On Thursday, shares of the watch and jewellery manufacturer and distributor plunged HK$1.075 or 51.81 percent to an intraday low of HK$1.00 before ending at HK$1.53.
Egana shares fell a further HK$0.27 or 17.64 percent on Friday to end at HK$1.26.

"We have ruled out plans to buy back shares at this stage after consulting our financial advisors," said David Wong, Egana's non-executive director. "It will look like we are speculating on our own shares if we do and it will spoil our image."
Wong said the company did not know who unloaded the shares, adding the company's directors were not involved.

Earlier in the week, chairman Hans-Joerg Seeberger placed out 60 million Egana shares to independent third parties at HK$2.05 per share before he subscribed to the same amount of new shares in the company.
Sun Hung Kai Investment Services Ltd was the sub-placing agent.
Proceeds would be used to expand the company's distribution network in Europe and the United States, Egana said.
Wong said the company plans to meet fund managers next week to discuss their concerns. He added that Egana's business expansion plans were still ongoing.

Wong said the recent fall in the share price would also pull down the price of the company's American Depositary Receipts, which began trading on the over-the-counter market in the United States as of October 30.
Each ADR share represents 50 deposited ordinary shares of the company.
